title: Combat Just Changed in Dragonwilds - Update 1.0.1
author: SuperStooob
chapters: Rune Arrow and Bolt Damage Buff
Dorgeshuun vs Blurite vs Rune Crossbow
Crystal Bow and Bow of Elidinis
Raid Skips and Ore Respawn Fixes
Enemy Aggro, Respawns and Combat Fixes
description:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds 1.0.1 brings new ranged special attacks, dedicated ring and amulet slots, a 40-slot inventory, and some easily missed changes to farming and raid routes.

Here’s what the update looks like in-game, including the rune arrow and bolt damage buff, Amulet of Glory nerf, Windstep plunge attack, and Kuldra’s ascension core drops. I also compare early crossbow results and check what’s changed for the Crystal Bow and Bow of Elidinis.

These are first-day comparisons. I’m doing a 24-hour stream this weekend for a full run-through with the update, then following up with more informed weapon and build recommendations.

transcript.text: Dragonwilds just changed your combat, equipment and inventory.
We got new special attacks, proper ring and amulet slots, eight extra
inventory spaces, and tucked away in the patch notes are some sneaky changes
that could affect how you farm resources and get through the raid.
I've jumped in to show you what it looks like in-game, what the new ammo
numbers are, and the changes worth checking before you head back out. I'm also doing a 24-hour stream this weekend,
so I'll be doing a full run-through with the update.
That will give me a much better idea of how these changes fit into the whole game,
and I'll follow up on the weapons and the builds after that. For now,
Let's start with something you can use straight away. So we finally got dedicated ring and amulet slots.
I don't know how long everybody has been asking for this one, but it feels like a long time.
You can equip both together, so choosing a ring no longer means giving up your amulet and vice versa.
My first thought was to go to the Ring of Recoil that reflects a portion of my damage back at the attacker.
There's also the Ring of Life as well. The experience rings, and there's more specialised options
like Ravana's Ring and the Abraxus Ring. It just gives you another effect to work into your setup.
And hopefully as more rings are added, there'll be more combinations to try.
And the Amulet of Glory has also been adjusted. Jagex says it was giving bonuses
above what was intended and they have been brought back down. Its tooltip still doesn't give a full numerical breakdown.
So when you're comparing damage with an older test or a guide, just remember that the amulet has changed as well.
So that's another piece of the setup we need to account for. Also, you probably noticed it from my last clip
that the inventory space now has 40 spaces instead of 32. That's more room for tools, ammo and food.
And of course, that pile of rubbish you decided might be useful one day. Now for the much awaited changes to ranged.
Each ordinary weapon subclass gets its own special attack. Shortbows have got Rapid Fire.
You're going to hop backwards and fire three arrows in quick succession.
That sits alongside the normal shortbow shots and existing movement attacks. Longbows get Power Shot.
Your character takes a knee, draws the bow, and fires a powerful shot at distance.
That's an option for opening a fight while you've still got time to line up the enemy. Ulv's
Longbow is one combination to look at because it already gets a bonus against the unsuspecting enemies.
Obviously, this is going to help out the Hunter's Stagbow as well. Crossbows get their special attack as well.
They get Heavy Bolt, which is a short charge and then a hard-hitting bolt. It's very similar to the longbow attack,
but importantly, the patch notes say it also applies enchanted effects on hit.
So with the Dorgeshuun Crossbow here, I hit a 176 and then the special I got 314.
But something really to investigate with this is the Dragon Crossbow with enchanted adamant bolts.
That could be a very good combination to investigate. The weapon's obviously the highest tier available.
It's got a special attack now, and the bolt effect is going off every time you use that.
So that's a combination I'm really looking forward to testing out further.
So aside from, like, these shiny new special attacks, This one was tucked away in the patch notes as well.
Rune arrows and bolts have now changed. They do a little bit more damage. The patch notes
list a 4.9-times multiplier for rune, compared with 4.2-times for adamant.
So on the tooltips I've recorded, rune arrows show 44 to 118, compared with 38 to 101 for adamant.
Rune bolts now show 88 compared to adamant's 76. Those are the ammo values.
Your final hit obviously depends on the weapon, target and the rest of your setup. Practical change
is that making rune ammunition now gives you a damage upgrade over adamant.
Unfortunately, this means I can't get away with just making adamant bolts anymore. I've got to make rune.
So that also changes the comparisons between crossbows.
And there's been big discussions about this ever since the Ascension
cores came out at tier seven. In the setup that I recorded,
we managed to get 176 as an ordinary hit with both the Dorgeshuun Crossbow, the Blurite Crossbow and the Rune Crossbow.
So the change that the Blurite Crossbow is benefiting from is the runite bolts, and obviously
matching on that hit doesn't settle how they perform over the full fight.
You've still got firing speed, special attacks, and ammunition effects to consider.
On the one hand, the Dorg uses bone bolts and can apply bleed to enemies that are susceptible to it.
Bone bolts are also cheaper for me to keep supplied than rune bolts. Blurite lets you change your ammunition effects.
Enchanted rune bolts can pierce through several enemies, while enchanted
adamant bolts increase the damage by draining some of your health. Of course, the Blurite and the Dorgeshuun
both have their speed bonus as well, which takes them above the Rune Crossbow.
So there's definitely some interesting combinations to test here. I want to know what you guys think in the comments.
Has this changed, or are we still considering the Dorgy the king of the bows?
We've also got Death From Above, the new plunge attack.
You unlock the skill-tree perk, get enough height, and attack to come crashing down onto an enemy. Windstep counts.
I tend to use that more than anything, so you can launch yourself up and drop straight onto them.
It's a nice refreshing way to open fights and it looks cool as well. I've confirmed
that it works with the Dragon Crossbow, but I think it is mainly just meant for melee weapons.
I still need to check which other weapons it works with, so I'm leaving that open for now.
The patch notes say that damage scales with your weapon. I think the weapon's tier may be a part of that.
The exact scaling does need testing, and if I'm being honest, I don't know how often I'm actually going to use this.
It is cool. And you know what? Sometimes launching yourself up into the air and landing on
someone's head is just enough reason to use it anyway.
We've also now got a completed quests tab with a short summary of each quest's outcome.
Also an opportunity for everyone to pause the video and notice the quests I still haven't finished.
I make guides, apparently I should watch some of those. So the biggest losers from this update is the Crystal Bow
and the Bow of Elidinis. They retain their own special attacks.
The Crystal Bow still shows Shattershot, which deals damage
in a cone and detonates after a delay. Elidinis keeps Lunar Rain.
Of course, their ordinary shots can still benefit from the stronger
rune arrows, but they haven't gained the new Rapid Fire or Power Shot. And obviously, when you get the Crystal Bow,
you're at power level three, which is a very long way from rune arrows.
So the Crystal Bow didn't even get an upgrade today, which is heartbreaking.
Then a few extra changes which would have been easy to miss. We've got Overdrive now
working on the Advanced Spinning Wheel, which gives you an option for speeding up that processing, which is nice.
Now we're getting Ultra Compost and larger compost buckets. Two massive upgrades.
What people have been asking for for such a long time. I haven't got those built for this footage,
but the additions are listed in the notes. We've also got
Divine Rock's cooldown has been corrected from 1,500 seconds to 1,800. That's 25 minutes becoming 30.
And they've also fixed some things to do in the raid,
including some of those Windstep-related skips, which I've definitely not been doing at all. No, not at all.
And also, ore no longer respawns when you teleport from the raid.
So if your usual resource route or raid route relies on one of those behaviours, you might need to change your ways.
Also, we've got enemy aggro range that's been reduced across the game,
and respawn timers have been extended, so clear areas stay clear for longer. That can affect how you move through areas
and how quickly you can repeat farming routes. Zogre farmers, please remain calm.
They fixed a few things with Enfeeble as well, which wasn't reducing the correct damage type,
and Blue Dragon's damage has been fixed where fighting from different heights
was producing inaccurate results, so both are worth keeping in mind
when comparing the older combat advice that I've given you guys to what happens now. And then,
one last thing: Kuldra's ascension cores. I got really excited when I saw this.
I thought we might be finally getting tier-nine cores, which would have meant taking
all those older weapons up another level. That would have been massive.
At this moment, though, it looks like she's only dropping tier eight cores.
Still useful because it takes some pressure off farming black dragons.
Obviously, if you're working through the dragon armour
and the weapon grind, you can now collect cores along the way, which is nice.
Hopefully, by the time you've got everything you wanted from Kuldra, you'll also have built up a decent supply
to bring some other weapons up to tier eight. It just gives those kills a little bit more value.
Obviously, if you've already finished that grind, the timing is impeccable. Congratulations. Back to the raid You go.
I'm going to see how this works across the full run
during this weekend's 24-hour stream. Tier nine would have been the exciting one.
Extra upgrade materials are still very welcome. And that's the update.
New attacks, new equipment, new combinations, more inventory space,
and changes to some of the methods we've been using to get through the game.
This weekend's 24-hour stream will give me a full run-through
with all of that in place. I'm going to be using the weapons for different fights,
see how the resource gathering feels, and find out what changes keep making a difference as I progress. After that, I'm
going to have a much better basis for the weapon and build recommendations.
And if you're joining the stream, you can watch me work all of this out in real time.
24 hours should be enough to learn something, right? Of course. No promises on my end. See you in the next one.
